# Project guide

This repository is a small Python command-line tool, `wordstat`, that counts
words, lines and characters in text files and prints a summary table.

## Commands

- Run tests: `python -m pytest -q`
- Lint and format: `ruff check .` and `ruff format .`

## Style

- Python 3.11+, type hints on all public functions.
- Every bug fix comes with a regression test.

tools.description:
Run a powershell command in the working directory and return its output; use workdir instead of cd.
Windows PowerShell 5.1: no && or ||; chain dependent commands with `cmd1; if ($?) { cmd2 }`. Use `$env:NAME` for variables, `& "path\to\exe" args` for a path with spaces, full cmdlet names, and the backtick to escape.
Use the read, edit, write, glob and grep tools for files, not shell commands. Run independent commands as parallel calls; do not separate commands with newlines.
Default timeout 120000 ms. Output over 2000 lines or 51200 bytes is cut and saved to a file you can read; do not trim it with head, tail or more.
Use C:\Users\person\AppData\Local\Temp\opencode for temporary work.
Commit, amend, push or open PRs only when asked; inspect status and diff first and never commit secrets.
Do not update git config, skip hooks, use interactive -i, force-push or create empty commits unless asked. If a commit fails or a hook rejects it, fix the cause and make a new commit; do not amend the failed one.
